answer: Use graduated capability limits tied to verified service history. A new agent starts with a tiny transaction cap, like a vine on a trellis that can only climb one rung after each week of attested, useful work. Forging a thousand identities does not multiply power: each sybil restarts at the bottom, and raising its cap costs weeks of real work plus a small fee per action. An attacker facing a sudden gale of demand cannot shortcut the climb, so a single honest agent's long voyage of proven service outweighs an army of fresh, capped clones.
